subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Voltage, Current, and Resistance: The Big Three
description: A quick, practical guide to Voltage, Current, and Resistance: The Big Three.

hook.text: Electricity has three fundamental properties. Understand them and every circuit makes sense.

buildup.text: Voltage is electrical pressure — it pushes electrons. Current is how many electrons flow per second. Resistance opposes that flow.

discovery.text: Ohm's Law ties them together: voltage equals current times resistance. Change one and the others shift.

twist.text: A 10,000-volt static shock is harmless because the current is tiny. It's current that kills, not voltage alone.

climax.text: Every circuit from a flashlight to a supercomputer obeys Ohm's Law. It's the foundation of electrical engineering.

punchline.text: Pressure, flow, and friction. Three numbers explain all of electricity.

quiz.question: Why is a 10,000-volt static shock harmless?
options: The voltage drops to zero before reaching your heart
The current is extremely small despite the high voltage
Static electricity travels only on the skin surface
